Routers and RESTful Routes

express.Router() as routes/web.php's equivalent, and mapping verbs + paths straight to functions.

In Laravel, every route lives in routes/web.php (or api.php), each line binding a verb + path to a controller method: Route::get('/tickets', [TicketController::class, 'index']). Express's express.Router() does the same job — a mini, mountable router — just organized one file per resource instead of one flat file, which suits a growing API better as more resources (comments, tags, users, ...) get added in later weeks.

Figure 1.5 mounts one router per resource onto the main app:

// Figure 1.5: aggregating per-resource routers (src/routes/index.js)
import express from 'express';
import ticketRoutes from './ticket.routes.js';

const router = express.Router();

router.use('/tickets', ticketRoutes);

export default router;

router.use('/tickets', ticketRoutes) mounts every route defined inside ticketRoutes under the /tickets prefix — so a route defined there as / actually answers at /tickets, and /:id at /tickets/:id. This is what app.js (Figure 1.3) was importing as routes and registering with app.use(routes).

Figure 1.6 is that ticket router — the actual verb/path definitions putting the REST conventions from earlier this lesson into code: a GET/POST pair on the /tickets collection, and a GET on one ticket via the :id route parameter.

// Figure 1.6: RESTful routes for tickets (src/routes/ticket.routes.js)
import express from 'express';
import * as ticketController from '../controllers/ticket.controller.js';

const router = express.Router();

router.get('/', ticketController.getAllTickets);
router.post('/', ticketController.createTicket);
router.get('/:id', ticketController.getTicketById);

export default router;

Two things to notice, both different from Laravel's routing:

  • No string-based binding. ticketController.getAllTickets is a direct reference to an imported function — not a class name + method name resolved by a container, like Laravel's [TicketController::class, 'index'].
  • :id is a route parameter, just like Laravel's {id} — Express just spells it with a colon. It shows up as req.params.id in the controller, covered next.
